name: Ion Channels
desc: A cross-section of a lipid bilayer — two rows of phosphate head-beads with fatty tails between, extracellular fluid above and cytoplasm below — studded with voltage-gated channel proteins; a depolarisation wave sweeps across the membrane and as its front reaches each channel the pore widens and ions pour through down their electrochemical gradient, sodium in and potassium out, flipping compartments while the rest jitter with Brownian motion, drawn as a textbook diagram, a grey cryo-EM density, an electric neon schematic, or a blueprint.

energy.doc: glow / potential-wash intensity — brightness of the membrane and ions

density.doc: number of channels and ions in the field

flux.doc: ion jitter and flow rate through open pores

wave.doc: speed of the depolarisation wave sweeping the membrane (0.15 still travels)

x.doc: pan across the membrane when magnified

y.doc: membrane height in the frame / pan when magnified

style.doc: coloured textbook diagram / grey cryo-EM density / electric neon schematic / blueprint

seed.doc: deterministic channel placement and ion pool
